design.name: One conversation, one canvas
design.principle:
Every screen has two panes, and each pane has one job. The conversation column on the left is the only place anyone talks to AnA. It holds one thread, one composer, one renderer (ConversationThread.tsx) and the only useAnaChat call left in client/src (V2App's). The canvas on the right is the only place work is shown: the document AnA is writing (streamed in live), a project, the Vault, a submission or a report.

Buttons in the canvas do their own job. To get AnA's help with something in the canvas, you attach it to the conversation. The product's functions are views inside a project's regulatory workflow (Plan, Evidence, Author, Review, Submit), not separate apps. The few things that really are organisation-wide stay as places: Vault, Submissions, Quality, Reports, My work and Documents. Each place uses the same component as the project's view of it, filtered to the project. There is no second implementation.

AnA proposes and the person decides. Anything AnA streams is a proposal until it is confirmed. Signing, freezing, filing to the vault and controlled export remain governed acts, each with a reason for change, an e-signature where required, and an audit-trail entry.
design.layout:
DESKTOP (wider than 1100px): the same grid on every route: sidebar | conversation | canvas.

- **Sidebar:** 264px, or 56px as icons. It collapses to icons automatically whenever the canvas holds something, as Claude's sidebar does, unless the person pins it open.
- **Conversation:**
  - With the canvas empty, it takes the whole width, with content centred at a 760px reading width.
  - With the canvas open, its width is clamp(360px, 30%, 520px).
  - A divider resizes it: role=separator, arrow keys move it 16px, double-click resets it. The width is remembered per person.
  - It collapses to a 40px seam that sits on the left edge of the canvas on every screen. The seam shows "✻ AnA" and an unread dot when a turn finishes while it is collapsed. One shortcut toggles it.
- **Canvas:** the rest of the width, minimum 640px. At 1440px, with the sidebar as icons and a 400px conversation, the canvas is 984px, so the editor's 940px minimum with comments fits.
  - The canvas header carries ⤢ (collapse the conversation to its seam, giving the canvas the full width) and × (close; the conversation re-centres).
- **No global top bar.** The conversation and the canvas each have their own header.

(1) THE AnA CONVERSATION (Home, or any thread with nothing open): expanded sidebar | conversation centred.
- **Header:** thread title (renamable), project chip ("in ONC-221" or "No project"), new-conversation icon.
- **Transcript:** turns; inline activity rows (the step record expands in place); compact document chips.
- **During a run:** one strip sits above the composer: "Step 2 of 5 · Pause · Stop". Typing during a run steers, in the same box.
- **Context chips above the composer:** what the canvas is showing (attached automatically, removable), attached files, and items attached from the canvas.
- **Composer:** one textarea. It has + (attach) and @ (app); Ask/Agent and the run policy sit in its footer, with the governed line beneath.
- **Home** is this screen with a new thread: a greeting, the composer and three quiet "continue" rows (last project, last document, My work count).

(2) A PROJECT: sidebar icons | conversation scoped to the project | canvas = the Project.
- **Canvas header:** project name, phase and filing; stage tabs Overview · Plan · Evidence · Author · Review · Submit. Respond and Lifecycle are hidden while their tools are out of release.
- **Overview:**
  - Needs attention: my tasks, review requests and signatures on this project, plus the deterministic readiness verdict.
  - Documents: DocumentList filtered to the project, with documents built by AnA marked.
  - Conversations in this project: ConversationList filtered to the project.
  - Project knowledge.
  - Linked Quality records.

(3) AN OPEN DOCUMENT: sidebar icons | conversation | canvas = the one editor (DocumentWorkbench in embedded mode, pinned to the document).
- **The canvas header is the workbench's own header,** not a second bar. It carries:
  - an "In this conversation (3) ▾" switcher;
  - title, document type and status (DRAFT / IN REVIEW / FROZEN / APPROVED);
  - a "v3 ▾" version menu;
  - a provenance line ("Drafted by AnA · model id · turn");
  - Download ▾ and Send for review;
  - ⋯ for Freeze, Sign, File to vault, Place into filing, History and Audit;
  - ⤢ and ×.
- **Body:** a collapsible 220px outline beside the section editor. Comments, history, sources, signatures, audit, project files and tasks open as a sheet inside the canvas; they already float at 1500px or narrower.
- The editor has no AnA tab.

(4) VAULT, SUBMISSIONS, QUALITY, REPORTS, MY WORK, SETTINGS AND EVERY OTHER SCREEN: sidebar icons | conversation (or its seam) | canvas = that screen at canvas width.
- The screen's own top bar or tab bar becomes the canvas header; QMS's separate top bar folds into it.
- Nothing collapses the conversation automatically, so it is in the same place on every screen. Dense screens use ⤢.
- The one exception is client-portal: an external client sees no AnA, by design.

1100px OR NARROWER: one pane at a time.
- The sidebar is an overlay drawer.
- The conversation and the canvas become one stack, with a segmented switch in the header: [Conversation] [‹item name›].
- Which pane shows:
  - Navigating to a place shows the canvas.
  - Sending a message shows the conversation.
  - An AnA-built document arrives as a chip in the transcript with an Open button and does not take over the screen.
  - "Ask AnA about this" switches to the conversation with the chip attached.
  - "Insert into §2.5.1" switches back to the canvas; this keeps today's D2 step 9.
- On a phone (600px or narrower) the layout is the same stack, full-bleed, with the composer pinned to the bottom.
design.anaPlacement:
AnA is talked to in exactly one place: the conversation column, to the left of the canvas, on every route except client-portal. There is one thread at a time (S, V2App's useAnaChat, which becomes the only call in client/src). It is drawn by one component, ConversationThread.tsx, which moves from being a surface to being the shell's column through a layout prop.

When the column is collapsed it is a seam on the same edge on every screen. ⌘K's "Ask AnA: …" and every attach button expand it and use the same composer.

If the canvas shows a different project from the one the conversation belongs to, AnA's write tools refuse. The column then offers "New conversation in ONC-305". Threads are already fixed to one project (routes/chat/threads.ts).

WHAT HAPPENS TO EACH CURRENT PLACE

- **Right rail (AnaRail, Shell.tsx:622-1548; A1 and the A2 seam):** deleted.
  - Transcript and composer → the column.
  - Run strip → the strip above the composer.
  - Work panel → the turn's inline step record.
  - "Working in" block → the automatic context chip.
  - Welcome starters → Home's empty state.
  - + menu → the composer's + and @.
  - "What AnA can do here" chips (Shell.tsx:1151-1168) → deleted; the canvas has real buttons, and attach covers the rest.
- **Full-page Conversation screen (B1):** no longer a destination. conversation-thread becomes a deep-link alias for "open this thread with an empty canvas".
  - Its side column (Progress and Artifacts, ConversationThread.tsx:1446-1478) is deleted. Progress shows inline in the turn; documents are in the canvas switcher.
- **Editor's own AnA, W (DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1419; pane 4533-4777; toggle 3702-3711):** deleted. The editor always takes the hand-off path it already takes inside the thread (askAna → the host's onAsk). The open document and section ride on each turn as context.
- **eCTD co-author middle pane, E (EctdCoauthor.tsx:335, 794-923):** deleted. The co-author becomes tree | document in the canvas.
- **RBM dock, R (Rbm.tsx:160, RbmSurfaces.tsx:363):** deleted. RBM's asks go to the column; RBM stays out of release.
- **ConversationThread's private fallback, C (:888):** deleted; tests pass a stub chat.
- **Home composer, C1 (Surfaces.tsx:264-402):** deleted. Home is the empty conversation.
- **Project home "AnA · co-author" card, C2 (ProjectHome.tsx:902-937):** deleted. Opening a project scopes the column to it.
- **Project home thread list, C3 (ProjectHome.tsx:965-1027):** replaced by one ConversationList used by the sidebar's Recents and by the project Overview (same GET /api/chat/threads, with a program filter).
- **Template library inline ask, C4 (TemplateLibrary.tsx:713-725, 737-739):** deleted. "Use this template" creates the document; "Ask AnA about this template" attaches it.
- **Launchers:**
  - Left-nav "Conversation" (A6) → "New conversation" plus Recents.
  - TopBar and account-menu "Get help" (A4, A5) → deleted. AnA is always on screen; the account menu gets "Help & documentation", which opens documentation, not AnA.
  - TaskTray "Triage my day" (A7) → a Home starter.
  - Live Drive steer box (A8) → deleted. Steering happens in the composer; the strip keeps Take over and Stop.
  - Run-strip steer input (A9) → the composer itself during a run.
  - Result: one typing box on screen, always.
- **Look-alikes:**
  - Insights' "Report builder" (D1) loses its chat shape. It becomes a builder panel whose satisfiable intents are buttons; free-form report questions go to the column.
  - AuthoringAiDraft (D3) is retired into "Draft this section" → the conversation → a tracked suggestion.

THE 77 ASK-AnA CALL SITES

The count is 77 grep hits for onAsk/ask( across launch and shell screens: 57 in v2 surfaces and 20 in quality/. A few are comments; the gate counts code sites at HEAD.

They stop passing free text. SurfaceViewProps.onAsk(text) is replaced by a typed door, ana = { attach(ref), draft(ref, instruction) }. Each site takes one of three dispositions:

(1) **Do the job.** The button calls the deterministic route or opens the thing, and sends nothing to AnA.
- "Open {§} in the editor" (BiopharmaProject.tsx:509, 743) opens the document in the canvas.
- Dispatch "transmit" (DispatchReadiness.tsx:646) opens the submission's Transmit step: a governed freeze plus §11.50 e-signature, never a chat message.
- Per-finding "Fix" (:620) opens the finding's target in the canvas with the finding attached.
- Licensing "contact sales" (:104) files a request through access-requests.
- The task board's automatic chat message after creating tasks (TaskBoard.tsx:1098) is deleted; a toast says what was created.

(2) **Ask about this.** attach(ref) puts a chip above the composer ("SOP-012 Document control", "Gateway posture", "Finding F-7"), expands and focuses the composer, and shows a suggested question as placeholder text. It sends nothing until the person presses Enter.
- This covers every "Ask AnA", "Explain…", "Summarize…", "Triage findings" and "Trace the evidence…" button.
- They share one label everywhere: "Ask AnA about this".

(3) **Draft.** draft(ref, instruction) sends an explicit drafting request with the target attached, and the result streams into the canvas as a proposal.
- Examples: "Draft with AnA", "Draft this section", "Ask AnA to draft the synopsis", "Ask AnA to plan this sequence", "Draft a status update".
- Admin's governed mutations (AdminAccess.tsx, 9 sites) are drafts for now. Their §11.50 confirmation renders in the column, which is now always on screen. That confirmation is the reason those screens had to keep the rail.

A shrink-only gate counts three things, each ratcheted down by the slices:
- free-text ask sites: 77 → 0;
- useAnaChat callers: 5 → 1;
- typing boxes that talk to AnA: 10 → 1.
design.canvas:
WHAT IT HOLDS: one item at a time: a document, a project, a place (Vault, Submissions, Quality, Reports, My work), or a record inside one of those.
- The canvas is the shell's page region. The URL names the canvas item, using the existing surface ids and navigation parameters.
- The conversation is the person's current thread, saved as it is today. Moving around the canvas never changes the conversation.

LIVE BUILD
- **Streaming the draft.**
  - When AnA calls draft_authoring_document, the gateway already buffers the tool input as it streams in (input_json_delta, gateway.ts:2812).
  - stream.ts surfaces that buffer as artifact_delta events. Each carries the title, section code and title, and the text so far. They are throttled to about 100ms and nothing is persisted.
- **Opening the canvas.**
  - The canvas opens on the first event.
  - If the person is editing something else, the canvas header shows "AnA is writing Clinical Overview — View" instead, and nothing is taken away from them.
  - The canvas renders the draft as it is written, marked "Proposed by AnA · not saved".
- **Confirming.**
  - The tool is class "confirm" (tool-authorization.register.json:1770). When the input completes, the confirmation renders on the proposal in the canvas, using the same GovernedActionSignoff component: "Save as draft in ONC-221" / "Discard". The turn shows one line: "Waiting for you to save Clinical Overview".
  - Once confirmed, the server persists the document: DRAFT, v1, with provenance (AnA, conversation, turn, model id).
  - artifact_draft then arrives with the authoringDocId, and the canvas replaces the stream with the stored record.
- **Declined or failed.**
  - The proposal is discarded, and the canvas shows the server's reason.
  - Streamed text is never downloadable, never fileable and never shown as a document (fail closed).
- **When this degrades.** If no fragments are available (deterministic gateway mode, or another provider), the canvas falls back to today's behaviour: the whole draft appears at once.
- **Revisions.** A second draft on an open document is a revision: tracked suggestions through row 50's anchored proposal, not a new document.

LIST: one DocumentList component over GET /api/authoring/docs, with three entry points.
- **Per conversation:** the canvas header's "In this conversation (n)". It filters on provenance.conversationId on the server, so it survives a reload. That fixes the risk that the 180-character tool trace (ConversationThread.tsx:107-167) loses the document id.
- **Per project:** the Author tab and Overview, filtered by programId, with a "Built by AnA" filter.
- **All documents:** the sidebar's Documents, filterable by project, status, author (AnA or person) and type.
- **Replaced by it:**
  - Project home's "Recent drafts", which reads a third store (c2c_document_sections).
  - The conversation's side-column Artifacts list.
- **Every generating tool writes an authoring document,** which finishes ANA_DOCUMENT_CANVAS.md decision 1. So there is one list.
- Artifacts Center leaves the navigation but stays reachable from ⌘K until its legacy rows are converted.

OPEN
- A transcript chip (AnaOutputs' card, one component for every host) has Open.
- Open shows the document in the one editor (DocumentAuthoring/DocumentWorkbench, pinned to that document) in the canvas, beside the conversation, on whatever screen the person is on.
- Removed: the inline card body, the separate "Open full editor" pane (.ct-canvas-pane) and "Edit in Authoring". There is nowhere else to go.
- The bridge that lets the conversation insert into the open document (EditorBridge) moves from DocumentCanvas's props to a shell context, because the editor and the conversation are now siblings.

DOWNLOAD: the canvas header's Download ▾ keeps two acts apart.
- **Working copy (.docx / .pdf), at any status:**
  - Rendered by the same renderer as the controlled export.
  - A watermark on every page: "WORKING COPY — NOT A CONTROLLED RECORD · doc id · v3 · DRAFT · downloaded by · UTC time", and "— working copy" in the filename.
  - Served by a new POST /api/authoring/docs/:id/working-copy. It writes an audit event (actor, version, content hash) but no authoring_export_history row, and does not re-baseline the document.
  - Requires the export permission.
- **Controlled export (.docx / .pdf / .xml): unchanged.**
  - Only for FROZEN or APPROVED documents, with the signature manifest; the server's 409 stands.
  - Otherwise the option is disabled and says why: "Freeze or approve to export a controlled copy".
- **File to vault: unchanged.** The reason is captured and the SHA-256 is recorded.
- The type-B .docx route (server/routes/c2c/exports.ts:125-129) retires into the working copy.

EDIT IN PLACE
- The one editor: section by section, with tracked changes, comments, citations, and citing from project files.
- AnA's answers and proposals arrive as tracked suggestions through the existing insertSuggestion/anchored-proposal path, attributed to AnA and to the turn.
- Nothing is saved until the person accepts. Each accept or reject goes on the chained record.

VERSIONS
- "v3 ▾" lists revisions and frozen or approved versions from the history tab, with compare.
- Restoring an old version creates a new revision and requires a reason.

PART 11
- Freeze, Approve and Sign sit under ⋯ and use the existing §11.50 dialog (re-authentication, meaning of the signature, reason).
- A reason for change is required for:
  - status transitions;
  - filing to the vault;
  - controlled export;
  - edits once a document is IN REVIEW (the existing reason tier).
- Audit opens the existing audit tab and "Download the record".
- AnA never signs or freezes; every AnA write is a proposal (P0-12).
- A confirmation given in the canvas writes the same chained turn record as one given in the conversation (D5). The slice proves this.

HOW IT TIES TO THE AUTHORING STORE AND THE VAULT
- The authoring store (authoring_documents and authoring_sections) is the one store for working documents.
- The Vault holds controlled records. File to vault writes a filed version with its hash and "Filed from {doc} v3".
- A filed record opens read-only in the canvas, with "Open the working document".
- Place into filing is unchanged; the submission's Contents tab shows the placed document.
design.workflow:
WHAT FOLDS INTO THE PROJECT: each stage tab hosts the same component, scoped to the project. Every old route stays as a deep-link alias.

- **Plan:**
  - the live schedule of events;
  - the Filings catalog, which becomes the "choose the filing" picker;
  - Program journey as the map, with its out-of-release links hidden rather than shown locked.
- **Evidence:** the Vault in project mode (the project's folder tree and records). It replaces "The document vault opens in its own workspace".
- **Author:**
  - DocumentList for the project.
  - New document ▾ (blank, or from a template). The Template library becomes this picker; template administration moves to Settings › Templates.
  - Protocol development and the Regulatory workspace (CSR board) open in the canvas as document-type views.
- **Review:**
  - One queue for the project's review requests, signatures due and tasks. The verdict and the signature happen on the document in the canvas.
  - Blocked: tasks and readiness are keyed on the integer project id, so this tab waits for that bridge (PROJECT_FIRST_PLAN). Until then it lists what it can and says what it cannot.
- **Submit:**
  - Submission Center in project mode. It reads the open project and does not ask for the programme again.
  - A sequence opens with these tabs:
    - Contents (Dossier map);
    - Author (eCTD co-author sections);
    - Validate (Dispatch readiness, the same deterministic gate);
    - Compile (eCTD compile);
    - Publish (Publishing);
    - Transmit (Gateway transmittals, with a governed freeze and e-signature).
- **Overview:** needs attention, documents, conversations, knowledge, and linked Quality records (PF-16).

WHAT STAYS AS CROSS-PROJECT PLACES: each is also the project's scoped view.
- **Vault:** controlled records.
- **Submissions:** the portfolio of sequences.
- **Quality:** SOPs, change control and QMPs, which are organisation-level by nature.
- **Reports:** Reporting & analytics plus compliance reports. "Report on this project" opens it filtered.
- **My work:** tasks, review requests and signatures due. It replaces Tasking, My Tasks and the top-bar task tray.
- **Documents:** all working documents.

WHAT LEAVES THE NAVIGATION but stays reachable from ⌘K or the account menu (nothing here is deleted):
- AnA Command. It folds in later: portfolio → Reports; pre-submission gate → Validate.
- AnA memory, Apps catalog, Artifacts Center.
- Review, until the project's Review tab can record verdicts and signatures.
- Audit trail, Part 11 console, admin, setup, licensing, billing, training.

THE CLIENT'S PATH: the same conversation column throughout, scoped to the project.
1. **Home:** "Start a Phase 2 IND for ONC-221." AnA proposes the project, she confirms it, and the canvas opens the project.
2. **Plan:** she picks IND in the filing picker and asks "what do we need for 0001?". AnA answers in the column and attaches the dossier map.
3. **Evidence:** she drops the CSR and the IB into the composer. They land in the project's vault folder.
4. **Author:**
   - She asks: "Draft the 2.5 Clinical Overview from the CSR and the IB."
   - The canvas opens and the sections write themselves as a proposal. She saves it as DRAFT v1.
   - She edits 2.5.3 in place, asks "tighten 2.5.4" with the section chip attached, and accepts AnA's redlines.
   - She downloads a working copy for her CMO.
5. **Review:** Send for review. The reviewer finds it in My work, comments, and records a verdict and signature in the canvas.
6. **File:** File to vault, with a reason. It appears under Evidence as a controlled record.
7. **Submit:** Submit › new sequence 0001 → Contents (place the document) → Validate (fix findings; each one opens in the canvas) → Compile → Transmit with e-signature.

These seven steps are the path D10 needs on production. The conversation never moves, and the project never has to be picked again.
design.navigation:
SIDEBAR, top to bottom. It is the same for every client type, and entries outside the release are absent, never shown locked.

- **Concept2Cure mark** → Home.
- **New conversation** → Home with a fresh thread. Home is not a separate entry: it is the empty conversation (greeting, the composer, and the continue rows for last project, last document and My work count). There is no other Home and no second composer.
- **Search ⌘K:** screens, projects, documents and conversations. "Ask AnA: …" sends into the column without navigating.
- **Projects.**
- **Documents:** working documents from the authoring store.
- **My work:** live count from /api/task-management/my-work.
- **Vault:** controlled records.
- **Submissions.**
- **Quality.**
- **Reports.**
- **Recents:** the last 8 conversations, each showing its title and project, plus "All conversations" (a canvas list, filterable by project).
- **Account, at the bottom:**
  - Settings: Organisation, Client type, Members & access, Identity & SSO, Templates, Setup.
  - AnA memory.
  - Apps & licensing: Apps catalog, Licensing, Billing & usage, Access requests.
  - Compliance: Audit trail, Part 11 console, Compliance reports.
  - Training.
  - Help & documentation.
  - Theme.
  - Sign out.

GONE FROM THE SIDEBAR
- **Client categories** → Settings › Client type. It never changed the navigation or AnA's context.
- **The "Science & intelligence" heading:** empty in production.
- **Explore** (AnA Command, AnA memory, Apps catalog, Artifacts Center, Conversation) → ⌘K and the account menu.
- **Quick access:** Recent Documents → Documents; My Tasks → My work.
- **Tasking** → My work.
- **"Project management"** is renamed Projects.

THE TOP BAR IS REMOVED
- The client-domain selector → Settings. Four of its five primary domains currently land a production customer on a "Not in this release" panel.
- "Get help" → removed.
- The task tray → My work.
- The breadcrumb → the canvas header.
- ⌘K → the sidebar.

ONE NAME FOR EACH THING
- **Submissions** (not Submission Center or Submit).
- **Submission readiness** is the Validate tab of a sequence.
- **My work** (not Tasking, My Tasks or Tasks & collaboration).

risks: Changing the UI invalidates parts of the D4 validation package. The OQ protocols were executed at 89ee3a81 with steps and screens that include the rail and the editor's AnA pane (for example OQ-AUTHORING). A change-control record is owed, and the affected OQ steps must be re-run after slices 4, 7, 9, 11, 12 and 15, before the pilot user files on production (D10).

Deleting a Canvas component again repeats the five-editor-generations pattern unless three things happen in the same change: ci:canvas-path is re-pinned, its selftest shows each new link failing, and each of D2's nine landed steps is mapped to a tested new home. The founder personally directed the 2026-10-01 version, so he should see slice 9 working before it lands.

The founder reverted a navigation restructure on the same day once before (2026-07-28: 'the shipped navigation wins'). The 2026-09-24 consolidation rule was 'keep what came from the design kits'. This design overrides both under the delegation of 2026-10-07. Mitigation: the AnA and canvas changes he asked for come first (slices 2-12); the sidebar restructure (slice 15) lands only after he has used the conversation-left/canvas-right layout in a real browser.

Canvas width: dense screens get less room on 1280px laptops with a 400px conversation. These include the Vault's three panes, Submission Center's tables, and the editor's 940px minimum with comments. ⤢ and the divider help, but each slice needs browser checks at 1280, 1440 and 1920; nothing should be assumed from the CSS alone.

One conversation across all screens could write into the wrong project. Threads are fixed to a project; when the canvas shows another project, write tools must refuse and offer a new conversation in that project. This needs its own test, or AnA could draft into a project the person is not looking at.

Test churn: about 15 test files reference AnaRail, and 6 anaDrivesWave tests assume the rail and the per-host drive controls. Migrating them behaviour by behaviour is slow, but skipping any of them silently drops coverage: history load error and retry, attachments, markdown, context honesty, run control.

registryModel.ts says it is 'GENERATED from the kit registry — edit the kit first'. Regenerating it would silently bring back the old rail. The decision must be recorded in the file, and any generator for the navigation arrays disabled.

Rule 2: the program must be framed as moving D2 (and the D10 path), with evidence under docs/evidence/D2-ONE-CONVERSATION/. Its 'workspace/*' files are components of existing launch surfaces, not a new surface, so the registered surface count must not grow (surface-registry-coverage test). A session that cannot produce browser evidence for a slice reports it blocked, not done.

Folding Review depends on the integer-project-id bridge (task and readiness stores) and on the split between the Review queue store and tasks: no client calls request-review. Until both are fixed, Review stays a separate canvas view reached from My work, and the project's Review tab reports blocked.

Live Drive semantics change: AnA now drives the canvas while the column stays put. The per-host drive controls (driveControlsRef) go away with W, E and R, so Stop and Take over must still end the one run. The anaDrivesWave tests need re-proving.

The conversation column is now mounted together with every canvas screen. Long threads beside heavy screens such as the editor or Submission Center may need a virtualised transcript. Measure this on the evidence machine before beta.
